To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The observed change in global mean surface air temperature over the last 20-30 years cannot be explained by the sum of the natural forcings alone, but can be explained by the combined anthropogenic and natural forcing.

(1) the current state of knowledge of natural climate variability is adequate for detection and attribution studies, (2) the current state-of-the-art of climate model simulations of anthropogenic forcings and climate responses is not yet adequate to support confident statements about attribution of observed climate change, (3) the current state- of-the-art is adequate to detect anthropogenic climate change, but (4) detection statements depend on which model's fingerprint is employed and on which time period of data are used.
